You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: HEAD responses served through http.ServeContent (or with no Content-Length) get a strong ETag computed from the empty body.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Late headers leak on the buffered path. `etag.go` `release()`/`finish()` send `w.Header()` at handler return, so headers set after WriteHeader(200) reach the client. The unwrapped handler drops them. Repro: `w.WriteHeader(200); w.Header().Set("X-Late","1"); w.Write(...)`. Wrapped response has `X-Late:[1]`, plain has none. The same happens after an implicit-200 Write. Fix: snapshot the header map (clone) when the status is committed, and send that snapshot.
- [blocking] A late ETag changes the outcome. Repro: `WriteHeader(200); Header().Set("ETag",`"late"`); Write("hi")` with `If-None-Match: "late"`. Plain returns 200 with body "hi". Wrapped returns 304 with no body and drops Content-Length and Content-Type. Same root cause as above. The snapshot fix covers it too.
- [minor] FEATURE_FLOW.md is an untracked file at the repo root. It was there before my probes and is not in the listed change. Confirm it is not part of this change.
- [minor] The doc comment says "Only a 200 response is buffered", but a GET/HEAD handler buffers until it commits a status. Wording only.
- [minor] `If-None-Match: "x", *` returns 200 (no 304). This is not reproduced as a spec violation: `*` is only valid alone, and the code's behavior is defensible. Not a blocker.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Post-commit headers reach the client when a panic follows WriteHeader(200). `syncHeader` runs only in release/writeNotModified, so the live header map still holds the late header. Probe `Recoverer(ETag(h))` with `WriteHeader(200); Header().Set("X-Late","1"); panic` returned `status=500 ... X-Late:[1]`. Criterion 11 is violated on this path.
- [blocking] Trailers are dropped. `syncHeader` deletes keys not in `committed`, so a trailer set after the body write is lost. Probe with `Trailer: X-Sum` set, body written, then `Header().Set("X-Sum","abc")`: unwrapped trailer `X-Sum=abc`, wrapped trailer empty. Fix by exempting keys listed in the committed `Trailer` header, or by passing trailers through.
- [blocking] Recoverer around ETag differs from Recoverer around the bare handler. Handler does `Content-Type`, `X-Handler`, `WriteHeader(200)`, `Write("partial")`, then panics. Unwrapped: `200 "partial"`. Wrapped: `500 ""` with the handler's headers. The request does not ask for this change in panic behavior; if the 500 is intended, it needs a test and a doc note.
- [minor] Flush with no body writes gives no ETag. A GET that calls Flush before writing and then writes a body gets no generated ETag. This follows criterion 10 but is not documented in the doc comment.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix one bug in /tmp/ff-eval-flp71_w4/workspace/middleware/etag.go (go-chi/chi v5 ETag middleware) found by review, with regression tests in middleware/etag_test.go.

FILES: middleware/etag.go (etagResponseWriter: WriteHeader, finish, setBodyHeaders, notModified, writeNotModified, release), middleware/etag_test.go.

BUG (reproduced): on the buffered 200 path, headers the handler sets after committing the status (after WriteHeader(200), or after the first Write which implies 200) are still sent, because release()/finish() send the live w.Header() at handler return. net/http ignores such late headers. Repros: (a) `w.WriteHeader(200); w.Header().Set("X-Late","1"); w.Write([]byte("hi"))` → wrapped response has X-Late, unwrapped doesn't. (b) `w.WriteHeader(200); w.Header().Set("ETag", `"late"`); w.Write([]byte("hi"))` with `If-None-Match: "late"` → wrapped gives 304, unwrapped gives 200 "hi" (and here the middleware must then generate its own ETag from the body, since the handler's ETag was set too late to count).

FIX: when the buffered 200 status is committed in WriteHeader, snapshot the headers (`w.Header().Clone()`). In finish() (ETag/Content-Length generation, If-None-Match matching, 304 header deletions) and release(), work from the snapshot, and before writing the status to the underlying writer make the underlying header map equal the snapshot (delete keys not in the snapshot, set the rest). Keep it simple. Same applies to Flush/Hijack-triggered release(). Also fix the doc comment wording: "Only a 200 response is buffered" → say the response is buffered until the handler commits a non-200 status, flushes, or returns.

CONSTRAINTS: don't change any other behavior; stdlib only; touch only those two files.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. `func ETag(next http.Handler) http.Handler` exists in middleware/etag.go with a doc comment explaining what it does, that it buffers the whole GET/HEAD response in memory, and that when combined with Compress, ETag should be registered before (outside) Compress so the tag is computed over the encoded bytes.
2. Non-GET/HEAD requests (POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, ...) are passed to next with the original ResponseWriter untouched: no buffering, no ETag, If-None-Match ignored.
3. GET returning 200 (explicit WriteHeader(200) or implicit via Write, or nothing written at all) with no ETag header set by the handler gets `ETag: "<hex>"` — strong, quoted, deterministic hash of exactly the body bytes.
4. A handler-set ETag (strong or weak) is never overwritten or modified.
5. The buffered 200 response is sent with all handler headers, status 200, the body, and `Content-Length` set to the body length unless the handler set Content-Length itself.
6. HEAD: same logic as GET, but no body is ever sent. If the HEAD handler wrote no body, do NOT generate an ETag and do not add Content-Length: 0.
7. If-None-Match matching per RFC 9110 weak comparison, comma lists, multiple lines, `*` → 304 with no body.
8. A 304 keeps ETag, Cache-Control, Content-Location, Date, Expires, Vary and other handler headers, but removes Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding, and Last-Modified when an ETag is present.
9. Non-200 final statuses pass through unchanged; first WriteHeader wins; 1xx forwarded immediately.
10. Flush, Hijack, Push, Unwrap forwarded as before; Flush during a buffered 200 releases and switches to pass-through.
11. Headers set by the handler after it commits the status (after WriteHeader(200) or the first Write) are not sent and do not affect ETag generation or If-None-Match matching — the response matches what net/http would send without the middleware, plus the generated ETag/Content-Length.
12. Tests cover every criterion, including regression tests for repros (a) and (b) above.
13. `gofmt -l .` prints nothing; `go vet ./...` passes; `go test -race ./...` passes.

CHECKS: while working: `cd /tmp/ff-eval-flp71_w4/workspace && go test -race ./middleware -run ETag`. At the end: `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`.
